title: Death an accident, jury rules ruled acc
article: Windsor police should receive more training in assessing vital signs and should contact ambulance dispatch directly, a coroner's jury into the death of Bryan Dukic recommended Friday.

The jury's verdict came after four days of testimony looking into the arrest of Dukic, 42, who died at Hotel-Dieu Grace Hospital, 9:43 p.m., April 5, 2006, within three hours of being detained by police.

The jury also recommended that ambulance services establish a protocol of questions to ask police in emergency situations, and that hospital emergency rooms be equipped with appropriate testing equipment for immediate results.
As well, the jury ruled the death an accident, caused by massive internal bleeding from lacerations to the spleen, made worse by liver cirrhosis and trauma to the chest wall.
Dukic family lawyer Gino Morga said the jury did as much as it could, given the constraints of its role under the Ontario Coroner's Act.
He said he will recommend that his clients sue Windsor police.
"My position right now is to recommend a lawsuit, if they choose to do so," Morga said. "I think there's grounds for a civil lawsuit, based on negligence, based on the delay in response."
Morga said though he can't say the arresting officers used excessive force -- as some civilian witnesses suggested during the inquest -- he feels certain police did not call an ambulance soon enough.

Dukic was arrested behind a Russell Street apartment building after being identified as a disqualified driver by police, who took him out of his van. Following an altercation with police -- witnesses said he was punched several times in the face and kneed in the torso -- his body went limp and he fell from a kneeling position to the ground.

Some witnesses told the inquest he did not resist arrest, while the arresting officers Const. Richard Sieberer and Const. John Ryan testified that Dukic was combative, yelled profanities and struck one of the officers, ripping his jacket.
Sieberer said he originally thought Dukic was "faking" when he fell over.
Morga said he doesn't think more testing for police is the answer. He thinks "common sense" was needed.
"I think the police get plenty of training," he said after the inquest ended. "The difference here has to do with the decision that was made and the time the decision was made.
"Independent witnesses from a distance, lay people who had no medical training whatsoever, were of the view that an ambulance should have been called much earlier."
Morga said evidence suggests police waited 45 minutes to call an ambulance after arresting Dukic.
But Windsor police lawyer Nancy Jammu-Taylor said the evidence showed police called within 15 minutes of Dukic's arrest, when they first realized he was in distress.
Jammu-Taylor said she will discuss the jury's recommendations with the police to see what might be the next step.

"The recommendations that have come back from the jury are very positive," she said. "If these recommendations can help in any way, shape or form, I know the Windsor police are going to consider them."
An investigation in 2006 by the province's Special Investigations Unit deemed that Sieberer and Ryan used reasonable force against Dukic.
